51608474.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to butyrophilin 3A1 (unknown origin) intracellular domain assessed as dissociation constant by ITC analysis
51608474.references_previous: C.H. Hsiao, X. Lin, R.J. Barney, R.R. Shippy, J. Li, O. Vinogradova, et al., Chem. Biol. 21 (8) (2014) 945–954, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chembiol.2014.06.006.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC Measurements: ITC was used to determine the binding affinities of the newly synthesized compounds. ITC was performed as described [14] using a nanoITC (TA Instruments).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Fig. 3. ITC of HMBPP and compound 6b, 6c, 6d and 6e. Left, titration of HMBPP or compound 6b, 6c, 6d and 6e into BTN3A1. Right, titration of BTN2A1 into preformed complex of HMBPP or 6b, 6c, 6d and 6e with BTN3A1 (data is representative of 3 independent experiments).
original_paragraph.Table 1 caption: a The binding parameters are obtained by independent fit using NanoAnalyze. Dates represent the mean ± SEM. Representative of n = 3 replicates.
original_paragraph.Results - 2.2 Biological evaluation: We first tested these compounds for the interaction with the intracellular domain of butyrophilin 3A1 using ITC (Fig. 3, Table 1). In this study, the positive control HMBPP bound to the BTN3A1 full intracellular domain with a Kd value of 6.1 μM, in line with our previously reported value of 1.5 μM [14]. Similarly, slightly stronger BTN3A1 binding was observed with compound 6a as described in our recent paper [25]. Of the new compounds, 6c also bound to BTN3A1 with a stronger binding affinity relative to HMBPP, like 6a. This suggested that additional electronegativity at the para position was not inhibitory to the compound binding to BTN3A1. On the other hand, binding was slightly weaker with compounds 6b, 6d, and 6e. Overall, all 5 compounds displayed significant affinity for binding to BTN3A1 full intracellular domain. The n values, which represent ratios of compounds, were higher than expected, as there is only thought to be one binding site available in this model. This may have resulted from variation in determination of compound concentration and/or the lower presence of cis isomers which are not expected to strongly bind to the protein. The binding of compounds 6(a-c) and 6e, but not 6d, exhibited more favorable entropy terms relative to HMBPP which contributed to their binding interactions.
